args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the v2.3.1 deploy, with error rate at 18% (0.18). Impact: elevated errors on checkout-api in production.

Remediation: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. v2.3.1-rc was not considered as it is staging-only and also unhealthy.

The initial rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet mixed — us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on the unhealthy v2.3.1. A retry of the rollback to v2.3.0 completed successfully across all regions.

Current state (verified): all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%.

Follow-up: determine root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and why the initial rollout/rollback was halted; investigate the orchestrator error. Do not redeploy v2.3.1 to production without validation.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did go through despite the timeout — INC-0001 is open. No retry needed (the idempotency key would have suppressed a duplicate anyway).

## Summary

**Root problem:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all three production regions with an 18% error rate.

**Rollback:** Rolled back to **v2.3.0** — the most recent release with a healthy production record. (v2.3.1-rc appeared "newer" in the release list but it's a staging build and also unhealthy, so it was correctly excluded.)

- The first rollback attempt **failed partway** with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet in a mixed state: us-east on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west still on the unhealthy v2.3.1.
- I verified the partial state, then **retried the rollback**, which completed across all regions.
- **Final verified state:** us-east, us-west, eu-west all on v2.3.0; healthy; error rate down from 18% → 0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, describing the failure, the rollback target and rationale, the partial-failure-then-retry sequence, and the verified recovery state.

**Worth following up on:** the orchestrator error that halted the initial rollback is unexplained and could affect future rollouts in this service — and v2.3.1's root cause is still unknown, so it shouldn't be redeployed to production without validation. Both are noted in the incident.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the current status and release history for checkout-api.

Current state: v2.3.1 is deployed in all three regions and is unhealthy (18% error rate). The most recent release healthy in production is **v2.3.0** (v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and also unhealthy). Rolling back to v2.3.0.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Current version 2.3.1 unhealthy. Most recent release healthy in production: v2.3.0 (seq 1). Note v2.3.1-rc is staging and unhealthy — not relevant.

Rollback to v2.3.0. That version was previously healthy in production, so no change-manager approval needed (the policy is about deploying a version that has never been healthy in production).

Then create SEV2 incident.

The rollback is a dependency for nothing else—the incident can be created in the same block? Actually the incident summary should describe what I did, so I should do the rollback first, verify, then create incident. But I can do them parallel... better to rollback first, confirm, then incident.

transcript.content: The rollback reported a partial failure. Let me check the current state before doing anything else.
transcript.reasoning_content: The rollback partially failed. Let's check the status.

transcript.content: The rollback halted partway: us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on the unhealthy v2.3.1. Retrying the rollback to complete it in all regions (v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production, so this is a routine rollback, not a new deployment).
transcript.reasoning_content: The rollback halted after us-east. So us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. I need to retry the rollback to complete it in all regions. Retrying rollback to v2.3.0 is safe — it's a known-healthy production version, not a never-healthy version, so no change-manager approval needed. Let me retry.

transcript.content: Rollback complete — all three regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate down from 18% to 0.2%. Now opening the incident.
transcript.reasoning_content: Healthy now. Now open a SEV2 incident describing what I did. Include the partial failure detail.
